runbooks.diagnosis: The zitadel service used to alias the PUBLIC ZITADEL_DOMAIN on opensme-net, so embedded DNS resolved the IdP FQDN to the zitadel container inside every compose service — where only plain :8080 listens. Every server-side OIDC backchannel (notes Django, invoiceninja Socialite, SOGo, synapse-setup, opencloud/paperless/camunda) died with connection refused at the exact step a browser login cannot recover from. Fixed by aliasing only auth.opensme.local and pinning host-gateway per dialer.
remediation: Ensure each OIDC-backchannel service has extra_hosts: ["${ZITADEL_DOMAIN}:host-gateway"] (traefik on host-net :443 terminates TLS and routes by Host)
Never re-add the public FQDN as a zitadel network alias
Verify with a curl to the token endpoint from inside the service's netns or a browser code-exchange

runbooks.diagnosis: Zitadel serves the JWKS at /oauth/v2/keys (its discovery jwks_uri) — the conventional /.well-known/openid-configuration/jwks path is not implemented and 404s, so every callback's ID-token validation fails with a 500.
remediation: Set OIDC_OP_JWKS_ENDPOINT: https://${ZITADEL_DOMAIN}/oauth/v2/keys in the OIDC service env
Verify the /.well-known discovery points at /oauth/v2/keys and that path answers

runbooks.diagnosis: A fresh notes database has no tables because the impress image entrypoint never runs migrations — the app starts against an empty schema and 'relation "impress_user" does not exist' appears.
remediation: Run python manage.py migrate --noinput inside notes-backend BEFORE starting uvicorn
For an already-broken boot: run the migrate, then restart notes-backend

runbooks.diagnosis: The impress image defaults to DJANGO_CONFIGURATION=Development, which appends django_extensions (absent from the image) to INSTALLED_APPS and dies at import. The image also ships a single impress/settings.py — a settings/ package module (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE) breaks it.
remediation: Set DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: impress.settings and DJANGO_CONFIGURATION: Production in notes-backend env
Do NOT set a settings/ package DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE — the image has one settings.py

runbooks.diagnosis: A 256M memory limit OOM-killed the Django boot (kernel SIGKILL): the app spawns 4 multiprocessing workers, each importing Django (~185M RSS), for a ~750M baseline. The limit was raised to 1.5G.
remediation: Keep the notes-backend memory limit at or above 1.5G
Check docker inspect opensme-notes-backend limits and dmesg for the OOM kill
Recheck after adding workers or importing heavy libraries — each import grows RSS

runbooks.diagnosis: notes-frontend attaches via network_mode: service:notes-backend; without an /oidc PathPrefix router every SSO path 404s on the static SPA despite a registered Zitadel client. Traefik 2.11 refuses to auto-link when a container defines multiple services, so explicit router→service links are required.
remediation: Keep the notesapi router rule Host(notes.<domain>) && (PathPrefix(/api) || PathPrefix(/oidc)) with priority 100
Keep the traefik labels on the netns-owner container (notes-backend), not the frontend
Ensure explicit traefik.http.routers.notesapi.service=notesapi links — auto-link will not happen
